primary_reviews.counterevidence: The following touch restores Daniel so the messenger can explain the same revelation.

primary_reviews.support: The full visual-bodily sequence reduces pressure to identify the figure from one descriptive clause.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: Messenger identity and canonical vision parallels remain explicitly undecided.

deciding_marker_or_seam: A hand raises Daniel at 10:10, repeated touch and reassurance restore speech and strength, the messenger explains his purpose and conflict, and his first-person support notice continues through 11:1; detailed truth begins at 11:2.
boundary_rationale: I retain 10:10-11:1 across the chapter boundary because the same messenger restores Daniel and explains why he came before introducing detailed truth at 11:2; 10:20 remains an internal purpose marker only.
rejected_alternative: The proposed split 10:10-19 plus 10:20-11:1 would distinguish restoration from purpose preface, but no section mark or speaker reset occurs at 10:19 and the complete encounter is the larger coherent route.
defensible_basis: Touch, commission, fear relief, repeated strengthening, Daniel's request to continue, purpose explanation, and messenger self-report form one interaction. The chapter seam does not interrupt the speaker; a new discourse formula does at 11:2.

source_observations.text: Behold, a hand touched me, which set me on my knees and on the palms of my hands.
“As for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to confirm and strengthen him.

primary_reviews.support: Speaker continuity carries 10:21 into 11:1, and the truth-announcement formula makes 11:2 a strong forward seam.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: The purpose question at 10:20 follows completed strengthening at 10:19 and can support two hydrated children.

challenges.claim: A whole 10:10-11:1 child may conceal restoration-dialogue versus disclosure-preface form.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Record 10:19-20 as an internal marker and preserve the split proposal as an append-only dissent.

primary_reviews.support: Repeated restoration and the messenger's purpose explanation are one preparatory interaction before the long disclosure.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: The shift at 10:20 is perceptible even though the speaker and encounter do not reset.

primary_reviews.support: The larger cross-chapter child avoids severing conflict language from Daniel's weakness and the messenger's commission.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: Prince and messenger identities, conflict mechanics, and historical referents remain outside retrieval authority.

deciding_marker_or_seam: The messenger's truth disclosure names three-plus-one kings, a rich fourth ruler, a mighty king, and the breakup of his dominion toward four winds through 11:4; the king-of-the-south register starts at 11:5.
boundary_rationale: I separate the four-verse prologue because it establishes succession and fragmentation before the disclosure settles into recurring north-south conflict, while the final-revelation parent preserves their continuity.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 11:2-20 whole would blur a compact succession prologue with sustained north-south cycles, whereas dividing the individual rulers would convert an introductory sequence into event atoms.
defensible_basis: Opening truth formula, concise succession, peak dominion, and fourfold dissolution form a bounded prologue. The directional title and relational conflict vocabulary at 11:5 initiate a different repetitive register.

source_observations.text: “Now I will show you the truth. Behold, three more kings will stand up in Persia. The fourth will be far richer than all of them. When he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up all against the realm of Greece.

When he stands up, his kingdom will be broken and will be divided toward the four winds of the sky, but not to his posterity, nor according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his kingdom will be plucked up, even for others besides these.

primary_reviews.support: The now-I-will-show formula opens the prologue and the king-of-south subject introduces a fresh directional sequence at 11:5.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: No speaker or scene reset intervenes, and the entire passage is one disclosure.

primary_reviews.support: Succession and fourfold breakup have a compact beginning and closure before the recurring conflict register.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: The prologue supplies the conditions for later campaigns and is not independently interpretable.

challenges.claim: The short prologue might be mistaken for a self-contained historical chart.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Attach 11:5-20 and the continuous 10-12 parent without mapping rulers.

primary_reviews.support: A bounded prologue can aid navigation if it is not converted into ruler, empire, chronology, or fulfillment identities.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: The fourfold imagery may invite harmonization with other Daniel visions or later texts.

deciding_marker_or_seam: The king of the south opens a directional conflict register at 11:5, followed by alliance, betrayal, campaigns, reversals, and successive replacements until the tax-collector successor dies at 11:20.
boundary_rationale: The conflict register stays broad because its many rulers and campaigns function cumulatively; I end only when a new contemptible successor is explicitly introduced, avoiding event-by-event historical atomization.
rejected_alternative: Retaining 11:2-20 would suppress the prologue-to-conflict reset, while separating every king, campaign, treaty, daughter, island turn, or successor would harden disputed historical mappings into the route.
defensible_basis: Directional titles, repeated turns, warfare and alliance cycles, and succession formulae accumulate as one compressed disclosure. The explicit in-his-place introduction at 11:21 launches the next focused antagonist movement.

source_observations.text: “The king of the south will be strong. One of his princes will become stronger than him, and have dominion. His dominion will be a great dominion.
“Then one who will cause a tax collector to pass through the kingdom to maintain its glory will stand up in his place; but within few days he shall be destroyed, not in anger, and not in battle.

primary_reviews.support: The directional ruler register begins at 11:5 and continues through repeated succession verbs until 11:20.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: Numerous internal action turns are textually visible but do not supply safe independent boundaries.

primary_reviews.support: The north-south cycles cohere as a dense middle movement after the prologue.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: Its length and changing actors can burden retrieval and encourage hidden historical assumptions.

challenges.claim: A long compressed register may be difficult to retrieve for a specific internal campaign.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Use internal navigation metadata without turning campaigns or rulers into chunk authority.

primary_reviews.support: The larger unit deliberately frustrates proof-texting of individual geopolitical details as settled predictions.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: Queries may still target one clause, requiring final-revelation hydration and identity guards.

deciding_marker_or_seam: An in-his-place successor begins at 11:21; deception, campaigns, covenant conflict, wise suffering, self-exaltation, end-time action, trouble, deliverance, awakening, and the direct sealing command continue until 12:4 before a new riverbank tableau.
boundary_rationale: I choose the larger 11:21-12:4 route to avoid encoding a same-ruler or new-ruler answer at 11:36 and to honor the temporal continuation into chapter 12, but preserve the 11:35-36 seam as genuinely unresolved.
rejected_alternative: The strongest rival splits 11:21-35 from 11:36-12:4 at the renewed king portrait; separate 11:36-45 and 12:1-4 children are rejected because twice-repeated at-that-time language carries the disclosure across the chapter seam.
defensible_basis: No new speaker or scene appears after 11:21, no MT section mark follows 11:35, and 12:1 explicitly binds its crisis to the preceding time. The command to seal at 12:4 closes the speech before Daniel looks again at the river.

source_observations.text: “In his place a contemptible person will stand up, to whom they had not given the honor of the kingdom; but he will come in time of security, and will obtain the kingdom by flatteries.
But you, Daniel, shut up the words and seal the book, even to the time of the end. Many will run back and forth, and knowledge will be increased.”

primary_reviews.counterevidence: There is no named actor change or MT section mark after 11:35, and local correlated witnesses cannot resolve the referent question.

deciding_marker_or_seam: Daniel sees two riverbank figures, one asks the linen-clothed figure how long, an oath and time expression answer, and Daniel's lack of understanding produces a second question ending with a pe at 12:8.
boundary_rationale: I keep the first question, oath answer, and Daniel's follow-up together because his second question arises from not understanding the first answer; the direct dismissal at 12:9 starts the closing response.
rejected_alternative: Keeping 12:5-13 whole would conceal the second question-answer reset, while ending at 12:7 would strand Daniel's question from the first exchange that occasions it.
defensible_basis: New visual tableau, first interrogator, solemn answer, and Daniel's responsive question form one dialogical round that hands directly to the final reply. The pe supplies a corroborating close after his question.

source_observations.text: Then I, Daniel, looked, and behold, two others stood, one on the river bank on this side, and the other on the river bank on that side.
I heard, but I didn’t understand. Then I said, “My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?”

primary_reviews.support: The riverbank seeing formula opens a tableau, and a pe after Daniel's second question closes this exchange.
primary_reviews.counterevidence: The two questions share the same vision and closing commission rather than opening unrelated scenes.

primary_reviews.support: First question, oath answer, incomprehension, and follow-up create a coherent opening dialogue round.

primary_reviews.support: The span keeps the time-times-half expression inside its oath and question context.

deciding_marker_or_seam: The speaker tells Daniel to go, repeats sealing, contrasts wise and wicked understanding, gives the 1,290 and 1,335 periods, and repeats a personal dismissal with rest and allotted standing at 12:13.
boundary_rationale: I separate the final response at 12:9 because it directly answers Daniel's second question and carries both numbers through his personal dismissal, keeping calculation-prone material inside its full closing commission.
rejected_alternative: Retaining 12:5-13 as one child would obscure the pe-supported second answer, while isolating either numbered period or final promise would sever them from sealing, refinement, and dismissal.
defensible_basis: Direct response, sealing reminder, moral-epistemic contrast, both numerical clauses, beatitude, and repeated go-your-way commission form the final answer. The personal ending closes Daniel rather than launching another unit.

source_observations.text: He said, “Go your way, Daniel; for the words are shut up and sealed until the time of the end.
“But go your way until the end; for you will rest, and will stand in your inheritance at the end of the days.”
